citation: Cui, L.E., Guerrero III, R.D., De Lara, A.V., Rebancos, C.M. and Faustino-Eslava, D.V. (2022). Diminutive Freshwater Fish in the Santa Cruz River System, Laguna, Philippines. Journal of Environmental Science and Management 25(1):48-56. https://doi.org/10.47125/jesam/2022_1/06

primarySource.sourceLocator: JESAM Vol. 25 No. 1 (June 2022), pp. 48-56; methods pp.49-50; Table 1 and results pp.50-51; conclusions p.55.

access.reviewMethod: Read full text in the official publisher PDF's web-text view on 2026-11-01.
access.directPdfRequest: HTTP 403 in direct-open check; the official web text view remained readable.
access.screenshotAttempt: The PDF screenshot route returned a cache-miss error; the table could not be visually checked.

survey.reportedSamplingPeriod: Three quarterly sampling periods from December 2016 through June 2017; exact visit dates are not listed.
survey.reportedStudyScope: Santa Cruz River System, Laguna; the paper describes upstream areas in Nagcarlan and Liliw, a midstream area in Magdalena, and a downstream area in Santa Cruz draining to Laguna de Bay.
survey.stationLabelConflict: The methods describe four municipality-linked areas including Magdalena, while Table 1 labels the four station columns Nagcarlan, Liliw, Calumpang, and Sta. Cruz. The article text available here does not resolve Magdalena versus Calumpang or provide a verified crosswalk to the existing single Sta Cruz River scope unit.
survey.methods: Electrofishing, seine and gill nets, and hand-net traps; representative specimens were taken to the laboratory and identified fish were sent to the UPLB Museum of Natural History for verification. The text gives no collection accession or voucher numbers.
survey.taxonSelection: The reported survey result is specifically for diminutive fish, defined by the authors as species with standard adult length below 100 mm; it is not a full fish inventory.

reportedResults.interpretation: Historical aggregate reported by the source for its study system and selected diminutive-fish scope. No taxon-by-waterbody or app record was transcribed.

qualityAndTaxonomyFlags: The table's machine-readable text is column-disordered and a visual page check could not be obtained. Do not transcribe station-level cells from that extraction.
The table contains source spellings/identifications requiring taxonomic review, including Glossogobius cf. illimis and Micropis brachyurus brachyurus; these are not normalized here.

The article describes Dawkinsia arulius as a first Philippine record and associates it with aquarium-trade introduction. That claim and the specimen identity need independent taxonomic and voucher confirmation before use.
The abstract gives a Shannon-Weiner range of 0.59-1.73, while the results discussion reports station values including 1.98, 1.91, 1.82, and 1.69. The discrepancy is unresolved.

reuse.policyFinding: The UKDR policy says authors assign article copyright to UKDR and permits specified personal-use exceptions; redistribution/use beyond those exceptions requires a written agreement.
reuse.disposition: Do not redistribute the article's species table or produce a structured public-app dataset from it without written permission and a separate visual/taxonomy review.

scopeDecision.reason: The source covers a multi-area river system and its station labels do not cleanly resolve to the scope registry's single Sta Cruz River lead. Do not assign all system-wide findings to that one unit.

nextActions: Request a station/site crosswalk and specimen accession details from the authors or UPLB Museum of Natural History.
Request written permission if structured species-level reuse is needed; otherwise prioritize independently reusable records.
Cross-check source names against an accepted fish taxonomy only after the specimen/source identification context is established.
nonClaims: This historical, size-selected survey is not a complete Santa Cruz River System inventory or evidence of present-day fish presence.
No station coordinates, river geometry, salinity, water-quality safety, catchability, natural diet, bait advice, or current legal rules are established by this review.
